html:
Workflow definitions, invocation and recovery

The current Workflow interface stores a reviewed request and starts a fresh ordinary Agent task for each invocation. Its HTTP routes accept saved_request_v1. The recipe package also retains native_intent and recorded_workflow_v1 implementations and storage contracts; these are not interchangeable payloads for the current Workflow editor or execute route.

Browser and editor flows trace draft previews, explicit saves, element-local submission keys, library invalidation and schedule binding. This guide owns the corresponding server contracts.

Artifact kind Stored meaning Execution boundary
saved_request_v1 Exact prompt, supported saved settings, independent context inclusion flags and owned asset descriptors. Current HTTP/native Recipe management uses ordinary durable tasks with fresh model routing.
native_intent Reusable goal, instructions, obligations, requirements and typed parameters. Compatibility helpers build a fresh model-led invocation and intersect capability ceilings.
recorded_workflow_v1 Reviewed tool/manual graph, dependency bindings, contract hashes and effect constraints. Retained runtime hooks constrain fresh native tool calls and receipt evidence; they do not replay source receipts.

Ownership and invocation

flowchart TD R[Reviewed saved request] --> V[Definition validation and execution hash] V --> S[Current definition and immutable revision store] R --> A[Optional owned context files] S --> C[Manual submission or scheduled occurrence claim] C --> G[Resolve saved Gateway intent] A --> I[Verify digest and materialize references] G --> M[Capture current model configuration] I --> T[Ordinary durable task] M --> T T --> Q[Existing admission queue and Agent runtime] Q --> H[Task status and fresh receipts] H --> P[Reconciled recipe run history]

RecipeRoutes validates the current API, coordinates launches and publishes recipes.changed. Saved-request helpers own source boundaries, settings normalization and copied context. The recipe-store factory selects the existing RAM repository when a Controller hub owns the path; standalone use retains SQLite. The existing task, schedule, Gateway and model-routing services retain their own execution responsibilities.

A manual invocation requires a reviewed recipe_revision and idempotency_key. The route derives a stable run ID from the recipe ID and key, then claims it before creating a conversation and task. An exact retry returns the recorded run; reusing the key with a different revision conflicts. Store admission prevents another open saved-request run for that recipe, including paused or waiting work. Scheduled occurrences enter the same recipe claim boundary through the shared scheduled launcher.

Saved settings retain operational intent, including selected Gateway IDs, accepted policies, parameter snapshots and a validated working directory. They omit source conversation/transport identities and model configuration. At each new manual or scheduled invocation, the Controller captures current Main/Helper and optional Vision routes and generation settings. Accepted tasks then retain that snapshot through queueing and resume. Recipe revisions pin the saved request and context; they do not freeze global model configuration for all future invocations.

Manual invocation sequence

The route checks that Workflows are enabled, the current definition is visible and the requested saved revision exists before returning an earlier submission. The idempotency key identifies a submission, not proof that its task completed.

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Workflow client participant R as Recipe routes participant S as Recipe repository participant C as Context and routing participant T as Task services UI->>R: Execute reviewed revision with submission key R->>S: Load revision and reconcile recent history R->>S: Look up stable recipe and key run ID alt Existing submission with the same revision S-->>R: Existing run and recovered task link R-->>UI: Current run response else New submission R->>S: Claim revision and reject overlapping open runs S-->>R: Pending claim R->>R: Create stable conversation and queued turn R->>C: Verify owned assets and resolve saved Gateway intent C->>C: Capture current model routes and materialize fresh references C-->>R: Saved policy plus current routing and new context IDs R->>T: Create ordinary queued Workflow task T-->>R: Durable task ID R->>S: Link task to claim R->>T: Queue or start through ordinary admission R->>S: Reconcile task state into history R-->>UI: Run, conversation, request and task identities end Note over R,T: Task creation and queue acceptance are separate effects

Definitions, revisions and persistence

The execution hash covers artifact kind/content, parameter schema/defaults and runtime contract version. Title, description and usage counters are excluded. Execution-affecting changes create a new revision; display-only edits update the current record without replacing an existing immutable revision snapshot. Current HTTP editing requires expected_revision; the lower-level compatibility update model permits an omitted precondition.

The active RAM repository publishes definition/revision changes, overlap claims and first-settlement counters atomically. Disk durability follows the shared Controller checkpoint protocol. Standalone definition updates and claims use immediate SQL transactions. Its history update reads the current run before acquiring the write lock, so its first-settlement counter check does not have the RAM transaction's concurrency guarantee.

Archiving hides a definition while preserving revisions and history. Current management reads at most 500 definitions, 200 run histories per recipe and 100 revision identities; embedded definition payloads show 30 recent runs. These page limits do not mean older stored revisions have been deleted. Recorded-workflow history cleanup retains 200 settled runs and preserves unresolved step evidence. RAM treats partial/interrupted runs as settled for this cleanup; standalone SQL prunes completed/failed/cancelled rows. This retention rule does not prune saved-request history or owned context files.

Copied context and source boundaries

The three inclusion categories—prior chat, attached inputs and previous tool results—are independent and default off. Historical capture stops before the selected user request. Its answer, its own results and later turns are excluded. Attached input references come from accepted request context rather than a live run's later steering additions. Tool results require a verifiable timestamp before the boundary; a terminal-run timestamp can serve as an explicitly labeled upper bound only when it is early enough. Missing or ambiguous boundaries reject capture.

Owned files live in workflow-assets beside the recipe database. Descriptors hold SHA-256, byte count, category and media type; definitions allow at most 16 assets, each at most 64 MiB. Writes use private temporary files, flush/fsync and atomic replacement. Reads verify both size and digest. Assets can be written before the recipe transaction, so a rejected definition can leave unreferenced owned files; this path has no transactional file rollback or automatic asset cleanup.

Deleting the source conversation does not delete committed Workflow copies. Materialization verifies each file and creates fresh attachment references for the new conversation. Chat/result copies are labeled historical reference material; they grant no current completion evidence or old execution authority. Re-enabling a category can reuse a retained revision's owned copy before trying the source again. That search is limited by the 100-entry revision listing.

The privacy boundary rejects detected secret values in saved settings and captured text using the canonical classifier and known source secrets. Binary attachments are copied as bytes and do not receive exhaustive credential inspection. Integrity checking establishes that bytes match the saved descriptor, not that their contents are safe or current.

Context data flow

The source request supplies the exact prompt and accepted settings. Optional history is bounded separately: prior turns and receipts must predate the selected request, while attached inputs can belong to that request's accepted context. For a newly authored draft, capture uses the recorded draft-time boundary and explicit input references. Preview computes summaries without writing owned files.

flowchart TD S[Selected request or authored draft] --> P[Exact prompt and saved settings] S --> B[Resolve capture boundary] H[Prior chat and tool receipts] --> B I[Accepted input references] --> B B --> F[Apply independent chat, input and result flags] F --> V[Validate selected sources and captured text] V --> A[Copy enabled categories to owned assets] A --> D[Digest and size descriptors] P --> R[Validated immutable Workflow revision] D --> R R --> L[New invocation] A --> X[Verify saved bytes] L --> X X --> N[Fresh conversation attachments] N --> T[Ordinary Agent task]

Capture and save sequence

The file copy precedes the definition commit. A final source-existence check can reject deletion during capture, but it cannot roll back already copied files. Missing settings on a historical request require an explicit choice to use current settings; optional source material is not silently substituted with newer content. Capture or validation errors end the save before the definition commit.

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Workflow client participant R as Recipe routes participant C as Source capture participant A as Owned asset files participant S as Recipe repository UI->>R: Save exact prompt and inclusion choices R->>C: Resolve source or current draft settings C-->>R: Accepted settings and prompt boundary R->>R: Retain or accept parameter-reference snapshot opt Any context category is enabled R->>C: Collect only selected historical categories C->>C: Check source boundaries and inspect captured text loop Each selected payload C->>A: Store payload by digest opt Digest file is new A->>A: Write private temporary file and fsync A->>A: Atomically publish digest file end A->>A: Verify size and digest A-->>C: Owned asset descriptor end C->>C: Recheck source conversation and selected turn C-->>R: Owned asset descriptors end R->>R: Validate definition and calculate execution hash R->>S: Save current definition and immutable revision S-->>R: Committed definition R-->>UI: Saved Workflow and recipes.changed event Note over A,S: File copies and repository commit are separate

Launch failure and recovery

Launch spans a recipe claim, conversation, asset materialization, task creation and queue admission. These effects are not one cross-store transaction. In manual invocation, failure before a task exists settles the claim as failed and records the failed turn. After a task exists, an exception can occur even though admission has already accepted work. The route leaves that claim open so retry/reconciliation can recover the task instead of creating another one.

History reconciliation follows the linked task and its user-visible native state. If the task link was lost, it searches the recorded conversation for a task carrying the recipe run ID. An orphaned claim from a different runtime instance becomes interrupted. Reconciliation scans the bounded recent-run page; it does not prove that every historical row has been reconciled. Read the task's outcome when deciding whether requested work completed.

Recovering an invocation

The following flow distinguishes the launch exception path from later history reconciliation. A claim with no linked task is searched by its conversation and recipe run identity before being treated as an orphan. Missing instance metadata or the current instance leaves an unlinked claim open; only a known different instance triggers the interrupted outcome. No branch below replays an old effect.

flowchart TD E[Manual launch exception] --> T{Task object exists?} T -->|No| F[Mark claim and turn failed] T -->|Yes| O[Leave claim open] O --> R[History or retry reconciliation] H[History read or next invocation] --> R R --> P[Inspect up to 200 recent runs] P --> S{Already settled?} S -->|Yes| K[Keep recorded outcome] S -->|No| L[Find linked task or matching conversation task] L --> A{Task found?} A -->|Yes| U[Repair link and project task or native wait status] U --> W[Update request identity, error and settlement] A -->|No| I{Known other instance?} I -->|Yes| X[Mark interrupted] I -->|No| Q[Keep open for reconciliation]

Scheduled Workflow sequence

Scheduling stores the saved prompt and pinned revision in the ordinary event system. Archiving or editing the visible definition does not remove that revision. Each claimed occurrence resolves the pinned settings against current services and captures current model routing. Manual and scheduled invocations share the recipe overlap check; creating a schedule does not reserve a future execution slot.

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Workflow client participant R as Recipe routes participant E as Event services participant S as Recipe repository participant T as Task services UI->>R: Schedule reviewed revision with timing fields R->>R: Verify assets and execution context R->>E: Create ordinary event with exact prompt and revision E-->>R: Created event R-->>UI: Schedule identity and pinned revision Note over E,T: Later occurrence uses the shared scheduled launcher E->>E: Claim occurrence and check legal acceptance E->>E: Create occurrence conversation and request identities E->>S: Load pinned definition E->>E: Resolve current targets and validate saved scope E->>R: Reconcile Workflow history E->>S: Claim recipe_run plus occurrence identity S-->>E: Accepted claim E->>E: Verify assets and materialize new references E->>E: Capture current model routing E->>T: Create ordinary scheduled task T-->>E: Durable task ID E->>E: Link event run to task E->>S: Link Workflow run to task E->>T: Queue or start through ordinary admission Note over S,T: Handled launch failures settle the claim

The diagram shows the successful occurrence path. The launcher records scope or overlap failures on the event occurrence, and settles a Workflow claim if one was created before asset or task-admission failure. Model snapshot capture occurs between those guarded blocks; an exception there is not handled by either block and needs later reconciliation. The event link is written before the Workflow task link; these writes are separate from task creation. The event architecture describes occurrence ownership and recovery, and the task coordinator owns execution admission after a task exists.

Retained recorded-workflow constraints

Graph contracts allow at most 64 ordered steps and 64 parameters, with a 128 KiB artifact limit. Dependencies must point backward, step IDs must be unique, and prior-step expressions must name both a declared dependency and one of its declared result pointers. Optional steps are read-only; required steps cannot depend on optional steps. Manual/checkpoint steps require an instruction and cannot supply result bindings.

Binding helpers recognize only exact {"$param": "name"} and {"$step": "step_id", "pointer": "/field"} objects. Strings are literal data. Fresh-result array traversal requires an unambiguous single item; it does not silently choose the first of several matches. Validation checks parameter names, finite numeric scalars, allowed constraints, a 64 KiB parameter payload cap, reference-only slots, current tool contracts and available capabilities.

The receipt recorder requires accepted completed work, owned successful receipts and provable dependency topology. It rejects uncertain effects, missing/ambiguous producers, unsupported bound-parameter capture and secret-bearing retained material. It links only declared structured result fields, excludes free-form prose outputs, preserves selected writes and rejects more than 512 source rows or an oversized dependency graph. Interactive Desktop/Browser/Clipboard action recording remains explicitly unavailable; no keystroke, clipboard or screen event subscription is installed by this package.

Runtime hooks persist a matched step as running before its effect. Further mutations stop on running/unknown outcomes or failed prerequisites, while permitted reconciliation reads remain available. Successful fresh receipts and required result pointers advance steps. Manual steps use the normal Ask User checkpoint. Adapter-owned applied-outcome proof can replace an uncertain step's evidence with a fresh successful read; model prose or evidence of absence cannot authorize a repeated write. Current permission checks still run at the ordinary executor boundary.

Receipt extraction data flow

The retained recorder starts with accepted completed native work and owned receipts. It proves a dependency graph from declared bindings, unambiguous structured result matches and resource ordering. It never asks a model to infer missing topology. All selected writes retain their earlier observations and effects as dependencies; unselected successful writes make the candidate ineligible.

flowchart TD S[Accepted completed native state] --> G[Check completion and unresolved work] R[Owned ordered receipts] --> G G --> P[Inspect successful tool receipts] C[Current tool contracts] --> P P --> D[Prove dependencies and unique result producers] D --> E[Follow completion evidence and required roots] E --> O[Preserve source order and selected writes] O --> B[Replace source identities with typed step bindings] B --> V[Validate bounded graph and inspect retained secrets] C --> V V --> A[Reviewable candidate and parameter suggestions] A --> K[Explicit caller saves a revision]

The capture wrapper returns a non-saveable candidate for expected extraction or shape errors. A candidate and its parameter suggestions are review data; producing them does not save a definition or invoke a tool. The current Workflow HTTP editor continues to accept saved requests only.

Recorded-step invocation and execution

The native entry point still recognizes a pinned recorded-workflow definition in accepted task context. It applies current capability policy before building the catalog and revalidating contracts, parameter references and targets. A scheduled retained artifact must also match its current definition revision. Current HTTP scheduling rejects these artifact kinds, so this branch is a compatibility boundary. The entry reuses a supplied recipe-run identity or creates a history claim, then marks it running before entering the Agent loop. Explicit native resume skips this initial invocation branch and restores the accepted checkpoint.

sequenceDiagram participant N as Native entry participant W as Workflow hooks participant L as Agent loop participant X as Ordinary executor participant S as Owned state and receipts N->>W: Revalidate pinned graph with current catalog and parameters W-->>N: Fresh prompt and reviewed execution context N->>S: Claim or reuse recipe history and mark running N->>L: Enter ordinary native runtime L->>W: Initialize or verify exact saved step graph loop Fresh execution-tool decisions L->>W: Check control surface and match tool step W->>W: Resolve dependencies from fresh owned results alt Reviewed pending step matches W->>S: Save matched step as running before its effect W-->>L: Permit matched call else Permitted extra read or notebook edit W-->>L: Permit without advancing a step else Workflow constraints reject the call W-->>L: Return guard error end opt Call is permitted L->>X: Execute under current policy and normal guards X-->>L: Fresh execution result L->>S: Retain receipt and result ownership L->>W: Observe receipt and optional adapter proof W->>S: Save step outcome and linked history end end

Permitted extra reads need not match a pending step. A matched step requires completed dependencies, the current contract hash, the reviewed effect and exact rendered arguments, apart from refresh/timeout hints. Internal Task Context notebook edits do not advance steps. Child/parallel execution surfaces are blocked by the workflow control guard, and successful finish requires every non-optional step to be completed. These checks supplement ordinary execution permissions.

Receipt outcomes and mutation gating

The running marker is saved before dispatch. If receipt handling never completes, that marker remains a reason to block further effects. The observer checks outcome uncertainty before success and keeps receipt references in step state; output bodies stay in the owned result store.

flowchart TD R[Receipt for matched operation] --> U{Outcome uncertain?} U -->|Yes| X[Outcome unknown] U -->|No| S{Successful receipt?} S -->|Yes| P{Required result pointers exist?} P -->|Yes| C[Completed step] P -->|No| F[Failed step] S -->|No| N{Execution explicitly false?} N -->|No| X N -->|Yes| A{Approval or credential wait?} A -->|Yes| Q[Return step to pending] A -->|No| F X --> M[Block further effects and allow reconciliation reads] F --> M C --> D[Dependents may match fresh calls] Q --> W[Normal approval boundary controls continuation]

Unknown outcome includes an explicit outcome_unknown status, or a possible remote effect without a successful receipt. The explicit non-execution wait cases are confirmation_required, credential_required and permission_required. A failed step remains failed; the uncertain-effect reconciliation hook below only addresses running or outcome-unknown steps.

Applied-outcome reconciliation

The optional proof arrives through adapter result metadata named workflow_reconciliation. The checked-in source contains the consumer but no adapter producer of that metadata; the contract tests supply synthetic proof. This diagram describes that retained hook. A fresh read alone can inform the Agent, but does not complete an uncertain step through this hook without proof.

sequenceDiagram participant L as Agent loop participant A as Adapter and executor participant S as Owned receipt store participant W as Workflow reconciliation Note over L,W: Running or unknown step already blocks new effects L->>A: Perform a currently permitted reconciliation read A-->>L: Fresh read receipt and optional applied-outcome proof L->>S: Persist fresh receipt and its ownership L->>W: Supply receipt plus adapter metadata W->>W: Require successful owned read and original operation match W->>W: Require applied outcome and equivalent structured outputs alt Proof qualifies W->>W: Point completed step to fresh read and retain original ID W->>W: Remove original operation from unknown markers W->>S: Save step state and synchronize linked history W-->>L: Downstream steps can use fresh result data else Missing or insufficient proof W-->>L: Keep unresolved step unchanged end Note over L,W: This hook does not retry the original mutation

Human checkpoint sequence

A manual/checkpoint step binds only when the question exactly matches its reviewed instruction and its dependencies are complete. Answer acceptance uses the normal request, checkpoint and authority validation. The Workflow hook records human confirmation without copying the reply into recipe step metadata.

sequenceDiagram participant L as Agent loop participant W as Workflow hooks participant H as Human-input boundary participant S as Owned native state L->>W: Ask User with exact reviewed instruction W->>W: Match pending human step and completed dependencies W-->>L: Bind step to Ask User operation L->>S: Retain waiting-user checkpoint H->>H: Validate submitted reply and current checkpoint authority H->>W: Mark matching waiting step human-confirmed W-->>H: Completed step without stored answer text H->>S: Commit reply context and step state together S-->>L: Resume through the ordinary continuation path

Retained native-intent helper

The older native-intent helper stores a goal, reusable obligations, requirements and an optional capability ceiling. Its capture gate checks for a truthy completion_accepted checkpoint; unlike the recorded receipt extractor, it does not independently recheck terminal status or prove a tool graph. Normal callers supply the runtime's accepted completion state.

flowchart TD S[Accepted completion checkpoint] --> C[Capture goal and reusable obligations] C --> R[Saved native-intent contract] P[Defaults and supplied parameters] --> V[Validate names, required values and basic types] R --> V V --> H[Reject historical requirement identities] A[Current capability ceiling] --> I[Intersect saved and current ceilings] H --> I I --> F{Explicit resume required?} F -->|No| N[Remove prior native identities and history] F -->|Yes| K[Retain supplied resume identities] N --> E[Ordinary model-led runtime] K --> E E --> O[Current decisions and owned receipts]

Its parameter checks are the older basic name/type contract; the recorded-workflow validator's numeric, schema and reference-only checks are separate. The convenience execute_recipe entry supplies the caller's request ID, uses saved/default parameter values and builds the goal from the contract; its prompt argument is retained for call compatibility and is not used to replace that goal. The native_resume_required flag preserves supplied resume identities. The native task entry also calls invocation directly with accepted parameter values.

Verification references

The saved-request fixtures cover inclusion boundaries, exact prompts, current model capture, overlap claims, revision pinning, task-link recovery and asset integrity. The recorded-workflow contracts cover capture topology, parameter bindings, schema migration and uncertain-effect guards. Runtime fixtures exercise fresh receipts and the current HTTP rejection of recorded-step payloads. The package README maps each implementation file to its responsibility. These fixtures use scripted models and temporary data; they do not certify a live deployment.
